operative_assumptions: Rewards in [0,1]; r2 depends only on the past action.
Graph strongly observable by self-loops; full decision set valid.
Theorem 3.2 imposes no lower-bound-theorem horizon restriction on this example.
Prescribed truncation feasible and entropy minimizer gives uniform first-round action.
The comparator is the best fixed arm on the realized reward sequence, as Eq.(1) specifies.

findings.claim: The minimizing truncated comparator satisfies ||v-v_epsilon||_1 <= K epsilon, used to obtain the epsilon K T term in Eq.(7).
findings.check: Use K=5,S=2,T=2,epsilon=1/(KT)=1/10, v=(1,1,0,0,0), v_epsilon=(17/20,17/20,1/10,1/10,1/10). All coordinates meet truncation, sum is 2, and L1 distance is 3/5 > K epsilon=1/2. Minimality follows because the three previously zero coordinates must gain 3/10 and selected coordinates lose the same mass.
findings.core_dependency: The false inequality is the source's stated justification for the per-round truncation bound, which yields Eq.(7)'s epsilon K T term in Theorem 3.2 and its inherited Theorem 1.1 guarantee. The independent positive-part repair is reviewer-supplied, not already given by the paper.
findings.counterevidence: The one-sided reward difference remains <=(K-S)epsilon<=K epsilon, proven directly by positive mass and rewards in [0,1].
